body: IPO May 2015 at $17 (10:1 split June 2022 -> ~$1.70). Rose ~6,480% to the Nov 2021 peak (~$169-176 split-adj) as the 'arms dealer' to independent merchants; Merchant Solutions (Shopify Payments, Capital, Shipping) overtook subscriptions — take-rate on GMV, not seats. Crash: 2022 bear market + post-COVID e-commerce normalisation + a capex-heavy logistics push (Deliverr bought for $2.1bn in 2022) returned Shopify to losses; stock -87% to $23.63 (Sept 2022). Reset: 10% layoffs July 2022, then May 2023 20% layoffs and sale of logistics/Deliverr to Flexport for a ~13% stake; stock +27% that day. Back to asset-light: positive operating income for 9+ quarters, FCF margins mid-teens+ [unverified]. New all-time high in late Oct 2025 (surpassing 2021; C$253 on TSX); 2025 was described as its best year. Split: 2015-21 mostly multiple on fast revenue; 2023-25 mostly margins/FCF growth. EARLY SIGNAL visible 2016-18: Payments attach rate rising, Plus enterprise merchants, app-ecosystem revenue — platform economics; in 2023 the signal was management abandoning capex-heavy logistics. Who caught it: founder Tobi Lütke (controlling shares); Baillie Gifford and other growth funds [unverified]. LESSON: a platform that drifts into capital-intensive operations loses its multiple; reversing that drift is itself a buy signal, and recovery to new highs took ~4 years.

data.early_signals: payments attach, Merchant Solutions > subscriptions; 2023 logistics exit
data.lesson: platforms lose multiple when they go capital-heavy; reversal is the signal

title: Shopify 2015-2025: ~100x, -87% crash, recovery to new highs
